> **Ritu cohort — Local/Early stage only.** This page repeats the Jiaxuan carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 analysis on the subset of patients with `tumor_stage == "Local/Early"`, leaving **N = 142** patients. `tumor_stage` is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set because it is constant within this cohort.
>
> **`steroids` is dropped from the adjuster sets on every page.** On this page it was already excluded because all 142 patients in the subgroup received steroids, making the variable constant and collinear with the intercept; together with an emptied `cancer_type_cat_7` "GI" level (cleared by `droplevels()` after the cohort filter) it made the design matrix rank-deficient and `cmprsk::crr` failed regardless of event count. `steroids` is retained as a descriptive row in Table 1.
>
> **Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page.** AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 5, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd) and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. **Read both models with their event counts in view** — 12 AKI and 7 CKD-composite events in 142 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See `RITU_PROJECT.md`.

# 1 Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup-ritu-carbo
# Force UTF-8 locale so kable captions and other strings render real Unicode
# (e.g. em-dash) instead of <U+2014> escape sequences.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8"))
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidycmprsk)
library(ggsurvfit)
library(gtsummary)
library(tableone)
library(flextable)
library(rvg)
library(officer)
library(patchwork)

# Output directory for downloadable Word tables
docx_dir <- "docs/tables/auc3"
dir.create(docx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Output directory for editable PowerPoint copies of every figure. A knitr
# plot hook (defined below) saves last_plot() to docs/pptx/auc3/<label>.pptx
# and appends a download link after the figure in the rendered HTML.
dir.create("docs/pptx/auc3", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pptx_dir <- normalizePath("docs/pptx/auc3", mustWork = TRUE)
pptx_rel_prefix <- "../pptx/auc3/"

.pptx_written <- new.env()
.pptx_pair    <- new.env()
.docx_written <- new.env()

# Relative path for Word-table download links from rendered docs/qmd/*.html
docx_rel_prefix <- paste0("../", sub("^docs/", "", docx_dir), "/")

# Save a plain data frame to Word and register it, so the chunk hook below can
# put a download link under the table. Named after the chunk label, as the
# PPTX files are; a chunk holding two tables passes a suffix for the second.
.tbl_docx <- function(x, suffix = NULL) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(invisible(x))
  name <- if (is.null(suffix)) label else paste0(label, "_", suffix)
  ok <- tryCatch({
    flextable::flextable(as.data.frame(x)) |>
      flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
      flextable::autofit() |>
      flextable::save_as_docx(path = file.path(docx_dir, paste0(name, ".docx")))
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) {
    txt <- if (is.null(suffix)) "Download Word table"
           else paste0("Download Word table (", suffix, ")")
    .docx_written[[label]] <- c(.docx_written[[label]],
      stats::setNames(paste0(docx_rel_prefix, name, ".docx"), txt))
  }
  invisible(x)
}

.save_pptx <- function(p, path) {
  tryCatch({
    doc <- officer::read_pptx()
    doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content",
                              master = "Office Theme")
    doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, rvg::dml(ggobj = p),
                            location = officer::ph_location_type(type = "body"))
    print(doc, target = path)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(filename) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(filename)
  pair <- .pptx_pair[[label]]
  if (!is.null(pair) && inherits(pair$default, "ggplot") && inherits(pair$fine, "ggplot")) {
    p1 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
    p2 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    ok1 <- .save_pptx(pair$default, p1)
    ok2 <- .save_pptx(pair$fine,    p2)
    rels <- c(if (ok1) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx"),
              if (ok2) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    if (length(rels)) .pptx_written[[label]] <- rels
    return(filename)
  }
  p <- tryCatch(ggplot2::last_plot(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(p) || !inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(filename)
  pptx_path <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
  if (.save_pptx(p, pptx_path)) {
    .pptx_written[[label]] <- paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx")
  }
  filename
})

local({
  default_chunk_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
    out <- default_chunk_hook(x, options)
    label <- options$label
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.pptx_written[[label]])) {
      rel <- .pptx_written[[label]]
      if (length(rel) == 2) {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download top plot as PowerPoint</a> · <a href="%s" download>📊 Download bottom (10 %% ticks)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1], rel[2])
      } else {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download as PowerPoint (editable)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1])
      }
      out <- paste0(out, link)
    }
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.docx_written[[label]])) {
      v <- .docx_written[[label]]
      out <- paste0(out, paste(sprintf(
        '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📄 %s</a></p>\n\n',
        v, names(v)), collapse = ""))
    }
    out
  })
})

# --- Sparse-outcome guard (Ritu cohort) --------------------------------------
# Restricting to Local/Early disease leaves several outcomes with very few
# events (90-day death = 2; thrombocytopenia grade 3 and the individual
# hospitalization reasons are in the single digits). A model that cannot be
# estimated raises an error, which would abort the entire render, so every
# table / row / figure helper is wrapped below. On success the output is exactly
# what the Jiaxuan version produces; on failure a short note is emitted in place
# of the table or figure. No model specification is changed.
.wrap_tbl <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e) knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-warning}\n",
    "## Model not estimable in this cohort\n\n",
    "Too few events among the ", nrow(dat), " Local/Early patients to fit ",
    "this model with the full adjuster set.\n\n",
    "Error: `", conditionMessage(e), "`\n:::\n")))
}
.wrap_row <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(time_var, status_var, label, ...) tryCatch(
    f(time_var, status_var, label, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      ev <- tryCatch(
        sum(as.character(dat[[status_var]]) == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
        error = function(e2) NA_integer_)
      tibble::tibble(
        Outcome = label, Model = "not estimable",
        N = NA_integer_, `Excluded (missing cov.)` = NA_integer_,
        Events = as.integer(ev),
        `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = "not estimable", `p-value` = "\u2014")
    })
}
.wrap_plot <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e)
    ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, size = 3.4, lineheight = 1.3,
        label = paste0("Model not estimable in this cohort\n",
                       "(too few events among the ", nrow(dat),
                       " Local/Early patients)\n\n",
                       strwrap(conditionMessage(e), width = 60,
                               prefix = "\n", initial = ""))) +
      ggplot2::theme_void())
}

# Table 1 via tableone. Factor-like columns (factor / character / logical and
# indicator columns of 0/1) are summarised as n (%); every other numeric column
# as median [IQR], except the variables named in `normal_vars` (mean (SD)).
# Categorical variables with any observed cell < 5 get Fisher's exact test.
tableone_mat <- function(d, strata = NULL, normal_vars = "age") {
  d     <- as.data.frame(d)
  vars  <- setdiff(names(d), strata)
  is_fl <- vapply(d[vars], function(x)
    is.factor(x) || is.character(x) || is.logical(x) ||
      (is.numeric(x) && all(stats::na.omit(unique(x)) %in% c(0, 1))),
    logical(1))
  fct_vars  <- vars[is_fl]
  cont_vars <- vars[!is_fl]

  if (is.null(strata)) {
    tab   <- tableone::CreateTableOne(vars = vars, data = d,
                                      factorVars = fct_vars, test = FALSE)
    small <- NULL
  } else {
    tab <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
      vars = vars, strata = strata, data = d, factorVars = fct_vars,
      addOverall = TRUE, test = TRUE, argsExact = list(workspace = 2 * 10^7))
    small <- fct_vars[vapply(fct_vars, function(v)
      any(table(d[[v]], d[[strata]]) < 5), logical(1))]
    if (!length(small)) small <- NULL
  }

  mat <- print(tab, nonnormal = setdiff(cont_vars, normal_vars), exact = small,
               showAllLevels = TRUE, missing = TRUE, printToggle = FALSE,
               noSpaces = TRUE, quote = FALSE)
  tibble::as_tibble(cbind(Characteristic = rownames(mat), mat),
                    .name_repair = "unique")
}

save_tbl_docx <- function(tbl, docx_name) {
  ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(tbl)
  flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(docx_dir,
                                               paste0(docx_name, ".docx")))
  invisible(tbl)
}

# Load the Local/Early cohort, then keep only carboplatin patients
dat <- readRDS("ritu_final_master.rds") %>%
  filter(platin_group == "Carboplatin", carbo_AUC >= 3) %>%
  # Ritu: clear factor levels left empty by the cohort filter above,
  # so the model matrices stay full rank (cmp_status_* excluded --
  # their 0/1/2 coding is relied on downstream).
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

# Create eGFR ratio: CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (unindexed) / Cockcroft-Gault
# Also create per-10 mL/min rescaled versions of cockcroft and CKD-EPI for
# reporting (HRs per 1 mL/min are clinically uninterpretable; convention in
# nephro-onc is per 10 mL/min — bio_agent confirmed). Adjusters keep raw scale.
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # Capped versions (for dose discrepancy calculations)
    cockcroft_cap125 = pmin(cockcroft, 125),
    # ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex_cap125 already exists in data
    # Ratio uses UNCAPPED eGFR
    egfr_ratio    = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / cockcroft,
    egfr_ratio_per10 = -egfr_ratio * 10,  # per 0.1-unit *decrease* reporting scale
    egfr_discrepancy = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft,
    # per-10-mL/min DECLINE reporting scale for eGFR discrepancy: HR for this
    # variable reads as the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower
    # discrepancy (i.e., when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is 10 mL/min farther below CG).
    egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10,
    # Sensitivity-analysis eGFR ratio (Section 16):
    # numerator = CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C only (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed)
    # denominator = CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine only (baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed)
    # per10 below is the per-0.1 DECLINE reporting scale.
    egfr_ratio_sens       = baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_ratio_sens_per10 = -egfr_ratio_sens * 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR (new primary exposure):
    # egfr_diff_pct = 100 * (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed - Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault
    # egfr_diff_pct_per10: HR reads as multiplicative change per 10 percentage-point DECLINE.
    egfr_diff_pct         = 100 * (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft) / cockcroft,
    egfr_diff_pct_per10   = -egfr_diff_pct / 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR for sensitivity analysis:
    # numerator - denominator = CKD-EPI 2012 CysC - CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, both unindexed.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens        = 100 * (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed - baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed) / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10  = -egfr_diff_pct_sens / 10,
    # Binary form of the same exposure: 1 when the cystatin C eGFR sits more
    # than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR. Reference level is ">= -10%".
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat    = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10, "< -10%", ">= -10%"),
      levels = c(">= -10%", "< -10%")),
    # Stricter cut at -30 %: a much smaller, more clearly discordant group.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30, "< -30%", ">= -30%"),
      levels = c(">= -30%", "< -30%")),
    # Intermediate cut, between the primary -10 % and the stricter -30 %.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -20, "< -20%", ">= -20%"),
      levels = c(">= -20%", "< -20%")),
    # Quartiles of the same continuous exposure. ntile() gives 1 to the most
    # negative quartile; Q4 (least discordant) is set as the reference level.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4     = factor(
      dplyr::ntile(egfr_diff_pct_sens, 4), levels = 4:1,
      labels = c("Q4 (least discordant)", "Q3", "Q2", "Q1 (most discordant)")),
    # "Survivor": still in follow-up beyond one year.
    survivor_365              = days_last_follow_up > 365,
    # Dose discrepancy uses CAPPED eGFR (already computed in ritu_data.qmd)
    dose_discrep_per25increase = dose_discrepancy / 25,
    abs_dose_discrep = abs(dose_discrepancy),
    abs_dose_discrep_cat = cut(abs_dose_discrep,
      breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("<25", "25-49.99", "50-74.99", "75-99.99", ">=100"),
      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    # Binary exposure for adjusted CIF curves (Section 14): 1 if patient was
    # over-dosed by 25 mg or more (actual - predicted >= 25), else 0.
    dose_discrep_ge25 = as.integer(dose_discrepancy >= 25),
    # Signed dose discrepancy = actual - predicted; 10 bins symmetric around 0.
    signed_dose_discrep_cat = cut(dose_discrepancy,
      breaks = c(-Inf, -100, -75, -50, -25, 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("<=-100", "-99.99 to -75", "-74.99 to -50",
                 "-49.99 to -25", "-24.99 to 0",
                 "0 to 24.99", "25 to 49.99", "50 to 74.99",
                 "75 to 99.99", ">=100"),
      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    cockcroft_per10 = cockcroft / 10,
    ckd_epi_per10   = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / 10
  )

cat("Carboplatin AUC >= 3 cohort N =", nrow(dat), "\n")
```

# 2 Actual vs Predicted Dose (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-dose-overlay
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
dose_long <- dat %>%
  select(record_id, carbo_dose_redcap, carbo_dose_cre_cys) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(carbo_dose_redcap, carbo_dose_cre_cys),
    names_to = "dose_type", values_to = "dose_mg"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_mg)) %>%
  mutate(dose_type = case_match(dose_type,
    "carbo_dose_redcap"  ~ "Actual (REDCap)",
    "carbo_dose_cre_cys" ~ "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)"
  ))

ggplot(dose_long, aes(x = dose_mg, fill = dose_type)) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.5, bins = 40, position = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Actual (REDCap)" = "#E31A1C",
                                "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)" = "#1F78B4")) +
  labs(title = "Carboplatin Dose Distribution (AUC ≥ 3)",
       x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Dose Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

Smoothed kernel-density version of the same two distributions (Actual REDCap dose in red, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys–predicted Calvert dose in blue). Easier to see location / spread differences without the histogram jitter.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-dose-overlay-density
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
ggplot(dose_long, aes(x = dose_mg, fill = dose_type, color = dose_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Actual (REDCap)" = "#E31A1C",
                                "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)" = "#1F78B4")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual (REDCap)" = "#E31A1C",
                                 "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)" = "#1F78B4")) +
  labs(title = "Carboplatin Dose Distribution (AUC ≥ 3) — density",
       x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Density",
       fill = "Dose Type", color = "Dose Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## 2.2 Signed Dose Discrepancy Distribution

Smooth kernel density estimate of the signed dose discrepancy (actual − predicted, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys). The area under the curve is shaded by sign — negative (under-dosed region) on one side, positive on the other.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-dose-discrep-hist
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
dose_vals <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_discrepancy)) %>%
  pull(dose_discrepancy)

dens <- density(dose_vals, n = 512)
y_at_zero <- approx(dens$x, dens$y, xout = 0)$y

dens_df <- tibble(x = dens$x, y = dens$y) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(x = 0, y = y_at_zero)) %>%
  arrange(x)

neg_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x <= 0) %>% mutate(side = "neg")
pos_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x >= 0) %>% mutate(side = "pos")
plot_df  <- bind_rows(neg_part, pos_part)

ggplot() +
  geom_area(data = plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = side), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = dens_df, aes(x = x, y = y), linewidth = 0.6, color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 25, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-250, 250), ylim = c(0, 0.010)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Signed Dose Discrepancy (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)",
       x = "Dose Discrepancy (mg) = Actual dose – Predicted dose",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

# 3 Table 1: Baseline Characteristics (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-table1-carbo
t1 <- dat %>%
  # Show the numeric KDIGO stage as a labelled factor for Table 1. get_ckd_stage()
  # collapses G3a/G3b into a single stage 3, unlike ckd_stage_cre / ckd_stage_cre_cys.
  mutate(ckd_stage_baseline = droplevels(
           factor(ckd_stage_baseline, levels = 1:5,
                  labels = c("G1 (>=90)", "G2 (60-89)", "G3 (30-59)",
                             "G4 (15-29)", "G5 (<15)")))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    age, age_cat, sex, race, ethnicity, cancer_type_cat_7,
    carbo_AUC, carbo_AUC_cat,
    ici, Bevacizumab, Paclitaxel, Pemetrexed, Doxorubicin, Etoposide,
    Gemcitabine, Pertuzumab, Trastuzumab, Docetaxel, other_chemo, Administered_alone,
    hiv_rpdr, thyroid, smoking, steroids, esrd_kt,
    cci, score, ecog_score, bmi, bmi_cat,
    pre_HGB_45days, pre_PLT_45days, pre_ALB_45days, pre_CRE_45days,
    baseline_cys_c, baseline_cre, cr_cys,
    baseline_cre_egfr, baseline_cys_c_egfr,
    ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex,
    ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys,
    cockcroft, egfr_ratio,
    # Long-horizon kidney variables (Sections 5.16-5.19 of ritu_data.qmd).
    # eGFR_CRE_baseline / ckd_stage_baseline are baseline; last_cre_days is
    # creatinine follow-up length; the rest are outcomes over that full window,
    # NOT censored at 90 days like every other outcome in this project.
    eGFR_CRE_baseline, ckd_stage_baseline, last_cre_days,
    aki, aki_any, ckd_incidence, ckd_incidence_any, ckd_progression,
    eskd_defination_1, esrd_kt_after_ici, eskd_composite, ckd_composite,
    # Delta eGFR vs baseline at fixed marks (Section 5.16b). Negative =
    # decline. Closest creatinine within +/- 45 days of each mark.
    delta_egfr_d90, delta_egfr_d180, delta_egfr_d360,
    delta_egfr_pct_d90, delta_egfr_pct_d180, delta_egfr_pct_d360
  ) %>%
  tableone_mat()

cap_t1 <- sprintf(paste0(
  "Table 1. Baseline characteristics, N = %d. Continuous variables are ",
  "median [IQR] except age, which is mean (SD); categorical variables are ",
  "n (%%). Missing is the percent missing in the cohort."), nrow(dat))

flextable::flextable(t1) |>
  flextable::set_caption(cap_t1) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  flextable::autofit() |>
  flextable::save_as_docx(path = file.path(docx_dir, "table1.docx"))

knitr::kable(t1, caption = cap_t1)
```

## 3.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)

Two alternative definitions of follow-up time shown side-by-side:

- **A — Raw days**: unrestricted calendar follow-up (median dominated by patients who kept returning for years).
- **B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days**: restricts to patients whose last-known contact was within 1 year of baseline.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-followup-desc
followup_summary <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, days_last_follow_up) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(days_last_follow_up)

fmt_med_iqr <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
}

fu_row <- function(label, v) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Interpretation                  = label,
    N                               = length(v),
    `Median [IQR] follow-up (days)` = fmt_med_iqr(v)
  )
}

v <- followup_summary$days_last_follow_up
followup_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fu_row("A — Raw days",             v),
  fu_row("B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days", v[v <= 365])
)

flextable::flextable(followup_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption("Follow-up time from baseline to last known status (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 cohort). Two alternative definitions.") |>
  flextable::autofit()
```

## 3.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the [ICI-CKD project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/ICI-CKD-/data_management.html)
and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd). Creatinine
for these comes from the Ritu_project RPDR pull (Oct 2026).

> **None of these are censored at 90 days.** A qualifying CKD episode has to be
> *sustained for ≥ 90 days*, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine
> follow-up. `aki` is restricted to events within 1 year. This section reports all
> of them descriptively; **`aki` and `ckd_composite` are the two that are
> modelled** — see the Fine-Gray section below. The rest are descriptive only.

**Definitions as of the latest revision.** `aki` is now restricted to events
**within 1 year** of baseline (`aki_any` keeps the unrestricted count for
reference and is not modelled). `ckd_incidence` uses a **> 25 %** eGFR drop;
`ckd_incidence_any` drops the percent requirement entirely; `ckd_progression`
now additionally requires a **> 30 %** further drop, where it previously counted
any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD
as progression and is why that count fell sharply.

`aki` is also not the same variable as `AKI_g2_90days` / `AKI_kdigo_90days`: it
compares each creatinine against the patient's own preceding 90-day median (or
2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation
below shows how far the two diverge.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/auc3/sec3_kidney_longhorizon.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-kidney-lt
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

kidney_lt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .kid_row("aki",               "aki_days",                    "AKI within 1 year (serial creatinine)"),
  .kid_row("aki_any",           "aki_days_any",                "AKI at any time (reference only, not modelled)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence",     "time_to_ckd_incidence",       "CKD incidence (>25% eGFR drop to <60, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence_any", "time_to_ckd_incidence_any",   "CKD incidence any (>=60 to <60, sustained >=90d, no % drop)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_progression",   "time_to_ckd_progression",     "CKD progression (<60 at baseline, further >30% drop, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("esrd_kt_after_ici", NULL,                          "ESRD / kidney transplant after baseline"),
  .kid_row("eskd_composite",    "time_to_eskd_composite",      "ESKD composite"),
  .kid_row("ckd_composite",     "time_to_ckd_composite",       "CKD composite (incidence + progression + ESKD composite)")
)

ft_kid <- flextable::flextable(kidney_lt) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(
    "Long-horizon kidney outcomes (N = %d). Not censored at 90 days.", nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_kid, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec3_kidney_longhorizon.docx"))
ft_kid
```

Creatinine follow-up actually available for these outcomes, and how the two AKI
definitions compare:

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-kidney-lt-fu
cat(sprintf("Days from baseline to last creatinine: median %.0f (IQR %.0f-%.0f), max %.0f\n",
            median(dat$last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(dat$last_cre_days, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(dat$last_cre_days, .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(dat$last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Patients with no post-baseline creatinine: %d\n",
            sum(is.na(dat$last_cre_days))))
cat("\nSerial-creatinine AKI (rows) vs 90-day KDIGO AKI (columns):\n")
print(table(`serial aki` = dat$aki, `AKI_kdigo_90days` = dat$AKI_kdigo_90days))
```

## 3.3 Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs Baseline over Days 1-90 / 91-180 / 181-270 / 271-360

Change in creatinine eGFR from `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, using the **median of
every creatinine eGFR inside each window** — days 1-90, 91-180, 181-270 and
271-360. Days run from `baseline_sample_date`. Built in Section 5.16b of
[Data Management](ritu_data.qmd).

> **Negative means decline.** `delta_egfr_d90` is eGFR at day 90 minus eGFR at
> baseline, so a fall in kidney function is a negative number — the opposite sign
> to `pct_drop` in the data-management pipeline.
>
> The windows are fixed and non-overlapping, so no measurement feeds two marks
> and every value drawn in a window counts toward it. A patient contributes to a
> window whenever they have at least one creatinine in it — the `n` column below
> shows how coverage falls off at the later windows.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/auc3/sec3_3_delta_egfr.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-delta-egfr
dgfr_marks <- c(90, 180, 270, 360)

dgfr_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(dgfr_marks, function(mk) {
  d  <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]
  dp <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_pct_d", mk)]]
  nv <- dat[[paste0("n_cre_d", mk)]]
  g  <- dat[[paste0("eGFR_CRE_d", mk)]]
  ok <- !is.na(d)
  q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
         median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
  wl <- c("90" = "Days 1-90", "180" = "Days 91-180",
          "270" = "Days 181-270", "360" = "Days 271-360")
  tibble::tibble(
    Window = unname(wl[as.character(mk)]),
    n = sum(ok),
    `% with a value in window` = round(100 * sum(ok) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `Creatinines in window` = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]",
      median(nv[ok]), quantile(nv[ok], .25), quantile(nv[ok], .75)),
    `Median eGFR in window` = q3(g[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR` = q3(d[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR (%)` = q3(dp[ok])
  )
})

ft_dgfr <- flextable::flextable(dgfr_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(paste0(
    "Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs baseline, N = %d. eGFR in mL/min/1.73m², ",
    "median [IQR] throughout. Negative = decline from baseline."), nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_dgfr, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec3_3_delta_egfr.docx"))
ft_dgfr
```

**Who is missing, and why.** The windows are only as good as the creatinine
follow-up behind them. The first two tables below show how many windows each
patient covers and which ones; the last shows how many creatinines those
patients had and how far their follow-up reached.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-delta-egfr-coverage
.k <- dat$dgfr_avail_d90 + dat$dgfr_avail_d180 +
      dat$dgfr_avail_d270 + dat$dgfr_avail_d360
cov_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  `Windows with a value` = factor(.k, levels = 4:0,
    labels = c("All four", "Three", "Two", "One", "None"))) %>%
  dplyr::count(`Windows with a value`, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(`% of cohort` = round(100 * n / nrow(dat), 1))

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(cov_tbl), caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "How many of the four windows each patient has at least one creatinine in, ",
  "N = %d."), nrow(dat)))

per_window <- tibble::tibble(
  Window = c("Days 1-90", "Days 91-180", "Days 181-270", "Days 271-360"),
  n = c(sum(dat$dgfr_avail_d90), sum(dat$dgfr_avail_d180),
        sum(dat$dgfr_avail_d270), sum(dat$dgfr_avail_d360))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(`% of cohort` = round(100 * n / nrow(dat), 1))

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(per_window, "per_window"), caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Patients with at least one creatinine in each window, N = %d."), nrow(dat)))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-delta-egfr-coverage-why
.iqr <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
}

why_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(0:3, function(k) {
  i <- .k == k
  tibble::tibble(
    `Marks covered` = paste0(k, " of 3"),
    n = sum(i),
    `% of cohort` = round(100 * sum(i) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `No post-baseline creatinine at all` = sum(i & dat$n_cre_post == 0),
    `Post-baseline creatinines, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$n_cre_post[i]),
    `Last creatinine, day, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$last_cre_days[i])
  )
})

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(why_tbl), caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Why marks are missed, N = %d. Patients are grouped by how many of the three ",
  "marks they cover. The last column is the day of their final creatinine."), nrow(dat)))
```


# 4 eGFR Distributions (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

## 4.1 eGFR Ratio distribution

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-egfr-ratio-hist
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
ratio_hist <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_ratio)) %>%
  mutate(side = ifelse(egfr_ratio < 1, "neg", "pos"))

ggplot(ratio_hist, aes(x = egfr_ratio, fill = side)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0,
                 color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Ratio (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)",
       x = "eGFR Ratio",
       y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## 4.2 eGFR Difference (sens) distribution

Signed eGFR difference (sens) = 100 × (CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C − CKD-EPI 2021
creatinine) / CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine, both unindexed. Concordance sits at 0 %.
Red bins are the negative side — cystatin C below creatinine, the
muscle-wasting direction. The dotted line at **− 30 %** marks the strictest of
the three cuts used for the binary exposures further down.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-egfr-diffsens-hist
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
diffsens_hist <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct_sens)) %>%
  mutate(side = ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < 0, "neg", "pos"))

ggplot(diffsens_hist, aes(x = egfr_diff_pct_sens, fill = side)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 2, boundary = 0, color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -30, linetype = "dotted", color = "#1F78B4", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Difference (sens): 100 × (CysC − Cr) / Cr",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0(
                          "Median %.1f %% of %d patients\n",
                          "Below -10 %%: %d (%.1f %%)   |   below -20 %%: %d (%.1f %%)",
                          "   |   below -30 %%: %d (%.1f %%)"),
                          median(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens),
                          nrow(diffsens_hist),
                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10),
                          100 * mean(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10),
                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -20),
                          100 * mean(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -20),
                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30),
                          100 * mean(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30)),
       x = "eGFR Difference (sens, %)", y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-100, 200, 10)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## 4.4 CKD Stage Reclassification — Creatinine vs Creatinine + Cystatin C

Every patient carries two KDIGO G-stages, both built in
[Data Management](ritu_data.qmd): `ckd_stage_cre` from `baseline_cre_egfr`
(CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine) and `ckd_stage_cre_cys` from
`ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys` (CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C). Both are indexed to
body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²), so the two stagings sit on the same scale
and the move between them is read directly.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-ckd-stage-xtab
stg <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(ckd_stage_cre), !is.na(ckd_stage_cre_cys)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys), droplevels))

ct <- table(stg$ckd_stage_cre, stg$ckd_stage_cre_cys)
knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(cbind(`Creatinine stage` = rownames(ct),
                           as.data.frame.matrix(ct))),
  row.names = FALSE, caption = sprintf(paste0(
    "CKD stage by creatinine eGFR (rows) against creatinine + cystatin C eGFR ",
    "(columns), N = %d. The diagonal is unchanged; right of it the cystatin C ",
    "stage is worse, left of it better."), nrow(stg)))

recl <- stg %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
    `Worse stage`  = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) > as.integer(ckd_stage_cre)),
    `Unchanged`    = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) == as.integer(ckd_stage_cre)),
    `Better stage` = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) < as.integer(ckd_stage_cre))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(`Worse stage`, Unchanged, `Better stage`),
                ~sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", .x, 100 * .x / N)))

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(recl, "direction"), caption = paste(
  "Direction of reclassification when cystatin C is added to the creatinine",
  "equation. A worse stage means the cystatin C estimate puts the patient in a",
  "lower eGFR band."))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-ckd-stage-sankey-fn
.stage_pal <- c("G1 (>=90)" = "#2E7D32", "G2 (60-89)" = "#1565C0",
                "G3a (45-59)" = "#EF6C00", "G3b (30-44)" = "#C62828",
                "G4 (15-29)" = "#6A1B9A", "G5 (<15)" = "#37474F")

# Hand-built Sankey: one polygon per creatinine-stage -> Cr-Cys-stage flow,
# node boxes scaled to their counts. Takes any staged subset, so the same
# figure can be redrawn on a sub-cohort without the code diverging.
.stage_sankey <- function(d, sub) {
  sk  <- d %>% count(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, name = "n")
  N   <- sum(sk$n)
  gap <- 0.055 * N

  # Node stacks: each stage a box, height proportional to n, separated by a gap.
  nodes <- function(col) sk %>%
    group_by(stage = .data[[col]]) %>% summarise(tot = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(stage) %>%
    mutate(ntop = lag(cumsum(tot), default = 0) + gap * (row_number() - 1),
           nbot = ntop + tot)
  ln <- nodes("ckd_stage_cre"); rn <- nodes("ckd_stage_cre_cys")

  lft <- sk %>% arrange(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys) %>%
    group_by(ckd_stage_cre) %>%
    mutate(l0 = lag(cumsum(n), default = 0), l1 = cumsum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(ln %>% select(ckd_stage_cre = stage, b = ntop), by = "ckd_stage_cre") %>%
    mutate(l0 = l0 + b, l1 = l1 + b)
  rgt <- sk %>% arrange(ckd_stage_cre_cys, ckd_stage_cre) %>%
    group_by(ckd_stage_cre_cys) %>%
    mutate(r0 = lag(cumsum(n), default = 0), r1 = cumsum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(rn %>% select(ckd_stage_cre_cys = stage, b = ntop),
              by = "ckd_stage_cre_cys") %>%
    mutate(r0 = r0 + b, r1 = r1 + b)

  fl <- lft %>% select(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, n, l0, l1) %>%
    left_join(rgt %>% select(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, r0, r1),
              by = c("ckd_stage_cre", "ckd_stage_cre_cys")) %>%
    mutate(flow = row_number(), pct = 100 * n / N)

  xlb <- 0.07; xle <- 0.22; xrb <- 0.78; xre <- 0.93
  tt <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 70); ease <- 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(pi * tt)

  # One polygon per flow: out along its top edge on a cosine ease, back along
  # the bottom. Tinted by the source stage so each origin stays traceable.
  rib <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
    list(fl$flow, fl$l0, fl$l1, fl$r0, fl$r1, as.character(fl$ckd_stage_cre)),
    function(id, l0, l1, r0, r1, src) tibble::tibble(
      flow = id, Stage = src,
      x = c(xle + (xrb - xle) * tt, xle + (xrb - xle) * rev(tt)),
      y = c(l0 + (r0 - l0) * ease, rev(l1 + (r1 - l1) * ease))))

  # Labels sit inside the box when it is tall enough, otherwise just outside it.
  nd <- dplyr::bind_rows(ln %>% mutate(xmin = xlb, xmax = xle),
                         rn %>% mutate(xmin = xrb, xmax = xre)) %>%
    mutate(big = tot >= 0.07 * N,
           lab = ifelse(big, sprintf("%s\n%d (%.0f%%)", stage, tot, 100 * tot / N),
                             sprintf("%s  %d (%.0f%%)", stage, tot, 100 * tot / N)),
           tx = ifelse(big, (xmin + xmax) / 2,
                       ifelse(xmin < 0.5, xmin - 0.012, xmax + 0.012)),
           hj = ifelse(big, 0.5, ifelse(xmin < 0.5, 1, 0)))

  fll <- fl %>% filter(pct >= 2.5) %>%
    mutate(lx = xle + 0.015, ly = (l0 + l1) / 2,
           rx = xrb - 0.015, ry = (r0 + r1) / 2, txt = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct))

  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = rib, aes(x, y, group = flow, fill = Stage),
                 alpha = 0.55, color = NA) +
    geom_rect(data = nd, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ntop, ymax = nbot,
                             fill = stage), color = NA) +
    geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(nd, big),
              aes(x = tx, y = (ntop + nbot) / 2, label = lab, hjust = hj),
              color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.95) +
    geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(nd, !big),
              aes(x = tx, y = (ntop + nbot) / 2, label = lab, hjust = hj),
              color = "grey15", size = 2.8) +
    geom_text(data = fll, aes(lx, ly, label = txt), hjust = 0, size = 2.9,
              color = "grey20") +
    geom_text(data = fll, aes(rx, ry, label = txt), hjust = 1, size = 2.9,
              color = "grey20") +
    annotate("text", x = c((xlb + xle) / 2, (xrb + xre) / 2),
             y = -0.055 * max(nd$nbot), fontface = "bold", size = 4.1,
             label = c("CKD-EPI creatinine", "CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = .stage_pal, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.11, 0.04))) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.15, 1.15), expand = expansion(mult = 0.005)) +
    labs(title = "CKD stage: creatinine eGFR vs creatinine + cystatin C eGFR",
         subtitle = sub, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-ckd-stage-sankey
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 6.5
.stage_sankey(stg, sprintf("Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 cohort, N = %d", nrow(stg)))
```

## 4.5 CKD Stage Reclassification — survivors only (follow-up > 365 days)

The same reclassification restricted to patients followed beyond one year
(`days_last_follow_up > 365`), the cohort the survivors models run on. Deaths
in the first year fall disproportionately in the low-eGFR stages, so the
all-patients figure above and this one need not reclassify in the same
proportions.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-ckd-stage-xtab-surv
stg_surv <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(ckd_stage_cre), !is.na(ckd_stage_cre_cys),
         !is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(c(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys), droplevels))

recl_surv <- stg_surv %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
    `Worse stage`  = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) > as.integer(ckd_stage_cre)),
    `Unchanged`    = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) == as.integer(ckd_stage_cre)),
    `Better stage` = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) < as.integer(ckd_stage_cre))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(`Worse stage`, Unchanged, `Better stage`),
                ~sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", .x, 100 * .x / N)))

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(recl_surv), caption = paste(
  "Direction of reclassification among survivors (follow-up > 365 days).",
  "A worse stage means the cystatin C estimate puts the patient in a lower",
  "eGFR band."))
```

# 5 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (unindexed, mL/min) (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> **These are the only two outcomes modelled on this page.** Both run on the
> long-horizon kidney outcomes built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of
> [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd):
> AKI is administratively censored at **365 days**, the CKD composite runs to the
> **last creatinine** (day 0 → last follow-up). Death at any time is the
> competing event in both, taken from `death_days_any` rather than the 90-day
> `death_90` flag, which cannot place a death in time beyond day 90.
> `death_days_any` is the union of the two sources that carry a death date — the
> RPDR `Date_Of_Death` when there is one, otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up
> date for a patient REDCap records as dead. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR
> with no date who is still alive in REDCap stays censored.
>
> **The exposure in both sections below is `egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10`** —
> `100 × (eGFR_CysC − eGFR_Cr) / eGFR_Cr`, negated and divided by 10, so every
> subdistribution hazard ratio reads per **10 percentage-point decline**.
> Cystatin C against creatinine alone, both unindexed. The two sections differ
> only in the kidney adjuster: creatinine eGFR in absolute mL/min here,
> indexed to body surface area in the next.
> All other adjusters are the project's standard set (Section 1).

Each table shows univariable (one variable at a time) and multivariable Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratios side-by-side. A Word version of each table is saved during render — the download link sits under its heading.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-fg-helper
.adj_set <- function(pre_labs, egfr_adj) {
  adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
           "cancer_type_cat_7","high_dose",
           "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
           "bmi","smoking","thyroid")
  if (egfr_adj == "cockcroft") adj <- c(adj, "cockcroft")
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi")   adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex")
  # Indexed to BSA (mL/min/1.73m2), as opposed to the absolute mL/min above.
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi_idx") adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys")
  # Creatinine-only CKD-EPI 2021, race-free. Unlike the Cr-Cys forms above
  # it shares no measurement with the exposure.
  if (egfr_adj == "cre")     adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed")
  if (egfr_adj == "cre_idx") adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) adj <- c(adj, pre_labs)
  adj
}

# fg_model: returns univariable + multivariable merged Fine-Gray table.
# If docx_name is supplied, also saves the table as a .docx in docx_dir.
fg_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                     egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                     docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- tidycmprsk::crr(fmla_mv, failcode = 1, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = tidycmprsk::crr,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3),
      method.args = list(failcode = 1)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_model <- .wrap_tbl(fg_model)


cox_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                      egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                      docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- survival::coxph(fmla_mv, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = survival::coxph,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_model <- .wrap_tbl(cox_model)

```

# 6 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²) (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> Identical to the section above in every respect but one: the kidney adjuster
> is **`baseline_cre_egfr`** — CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine **indexed
> to body surface area, mL/min/1.73m²** — where the section above uses
> `baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed`, the same estimate in absolute mL/min.
>
> Same exposure (`egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10`, per 10 percentage-point decline),
> same two outcomes, same competing event, same remaining covariates. The two
> sections therefore isolate what the BSA indexing of the adjuster does. The two
> forms correlate at 0.84, so they are related but not interchangeable.
>
> Cockcroft-Gault is no longer an adjuster in either section.

# 7 Survivors Cohort — Follow-up > 365 Days (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> The Fine-Gray models above, rerun on patients still in follow-up beyond one
> year (`days_last_follow_up > 365`). Adjusted for **`baseline_cre_egfr`**
> (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²); same exposure and competing event, only the cohort
> changes.
>
> **This conditions on a post-baseline characteristic.** Surviving and staying in
> follow-up past a year is partly a consequence of the kidney trajectory being
> modelled, so this subset is not a random sample and these estimates are not
> directly comparable with the full-cohort ones above. Read it as a restriction
> analysis, not a sensitivity analysis.

# 8 Binary eGFR Difference (sens) — AKI and CKD Composite (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> The same two outcomes and the same adjusters as the Fine-Gray sections above,
> with the exposure entered as a **binary split** rather than per 10
> percentage-point decline.
>
> - `egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat` splits at **− 10 %** — `< -10%` means the cystatin C
>   eGFR sits more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; `>= -10%` is the
>   reference.
> - `egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20` splits at **− 20 %**, an intermediate cut.
> - `egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30` splits at **− 30 %**, a smaller and more clearly
>   discordant group.
>
> Each subdistribution hazard ratio is therefore for the exposed group **against
> its reference group**, not per unit. Death at any time is the competing event
> and the kidney adjuster is `baseline_cre_egfr` (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²), as
> in the sections above.

## 8.1 Prevalence of the three cuts

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-bin-prev
.cut_row <- function(v, lab) tibble::tibble(
  Cut = lab, Exposed = sum(v), Unexposed = sum(!v),
  `% exposed` = round(100 * mean(v), 1),
  `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[v]  == 1),
  `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!v] == 1),
  `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[v]  == 1),
  `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!v] == 1))

cut_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat   == "< -10%", "< -10% (primary)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20 == "< -20%", "< -20% (intermediate)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30 == "< -30%", "< -30% (stricter)"))

knitr::kable(cut_tbl, caption = sprintf(
  "Prevalence of the three binary cuts, N = %d. Median eGFR difference (sens) %.1f %%.",
  nrow(dat), median(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-binsurv-enter
dat_full_cohort <- dat
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

binsurv <- purrr::map_dfr(
  list(c("< -10%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat"),
       c("< -20%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20"),
       c("< -30%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30")),
  function(z) {
    e <- dat[[z[2]]] == z[1]
    tibble::tibble(Cut = z[1], `n survivors` = nrow(dat),
                   Exposed = sum(e), Unexposed = sum(!e),
                   `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[e]  == 1),
                   `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!e] == 1),
                   `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[e]  == 1),
                   `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!e] == 1))
  })
knitr::kable(binsurv, caption = sprintf(
  "Survivors cohort: %d of %d patients. Exposed-group event counts behind the six models below.",
  nrow(dat), nrow(dat_full_cohort)))
```

# 10 Paper (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-paper-stats
#| include: false
n_excess  <- sum(dat$dose_discrep_ge25 == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

pct_excess <- round(n_excess / n_with_dx * 100, 1)
```

A total of `r n_excess` (`r pct_excess`%) patients received an excess dose of carboplatin, defined as ≥ 25 mg higher than the dose that would have been predicted using the CKD-EPI eGFR~CR-CYS~ equation adjusted for actual BSA.

(Denominator: `r n_with_dx` carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 patients with a computable predicted dose.)


# 11 360-Day Delta eGFR on the Binary eGFR Difference (sens) (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> The outcome is `delta_egfr_d360` — the median creatinine eGFR over days
> 271-360 minus baseline, in mL/min/1.73m², **negative = decline** (see the
> Delta eGFR table above). Only patients with at least one creatinine in that
> window contribute, so every model in this section is complete-case on that
> variable and its n is well below the cohort.
>
> Both cuts of `egfr_diff_pct_sens` are reported: the primary one at **− 10 %**
> and the stricter one at **− 30 %**. `< -10%` means the cystatin C eGFR sits
> more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; `>= -10%` is the reference level.

## 11.1 360-day delta eGFR by group — cut at − 10 %

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-cat-groups
.grp_row <- function(d, lab) {
  v <- d$delta_egfr_d360[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_d360)]
  p <- d$delta_egfr_pct_d360[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_pct_d360)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Group = lab, n = length(v),
    `Delta eGFR, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(v), sd(v)),
    `Delta eGFR, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(v), quantile(v, .25), quantile(v, .75)),
    `Delta eGFR %, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(p), quantile(p, .25), quantile(p, .75)))
}
d0 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == ">= -10%")
d1 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == "< -10%")
grp_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(.grp_row(d0, ">= -10% (reference)"), .grp_row(d1, "< -10%"))

.wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(delta_egfr_d360 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
.tt <- tryCatch(t.test(delta_egfr_d360 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(grp_tbl), caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "360-day delta eGFR by binary eGFR difference (sens). Negative = decline. ",
  "Wilcoxon p = %s; Welch t-test p = %s."),
  if (is.null(.wt)) "—" else format.pval(.wt$p.value, digits = 3),
  if (is.null(.tt)) "—" else format.pval(.tt$p.value, digits = 3)))
```

## 11.2 Linear model — cut at − 10 % (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3, all patients)

Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models,
including the same kidney adjuster — `baseline_cre_egfr`, CKD-EPI 2021
race-free creatinine indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of
365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on `< -10%` means that group
declined further.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/auc3/sec11_lm_d360.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-cat-lm
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d360 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "cre_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d360 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d360", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d360,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
lm_d360 <- .wrap_tbl(lm_d360)

lm_d360("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat", docx_name = "sec11_lm_d360")
```

# 12 Quartiles of eGFR Difference (sens) as the Exposure (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> The same continuous exposure as the Fine-Gray sections above, entered as
> **quartiles** instead of a binary cut or a per-10-point slope.
> `egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4` is built with `dplyr::ntile()`, so Q1 holds the most
> discordant quarter (cystatin C furthest below creatinine) and Q4 the least.
> **Q4 is the reference level**, so each ratio reads against the least
> discordant quarter and a value above 1 means more discordance carries more
> risk.
>
> Same two outcomes, same competing event (death at any time), same
> multivariable set and the same kidney adjuster `baseline_cre_egfr` as
> everywhere else on this page. Three dummy terms replace one, so these models
> spend two more degrees of freedom than the binary ones on the same events.

```{r}
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Range (%)` = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f",
                                  min(egfr_diff_pct_sens), max(egfr_diff_pct_sens)),
            `Median (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", median(egfr_diff_pct_sens)),
            `AKI events` = sum(cmp_status_aki_365 == 1),
            `CKD events` = sum(cmp_status_ckd_composite == 1),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(q_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Quartiles of eGFR difference (sens), N = %d with a non-missing value. ",
  "Q4 (least discordant) is the reference level in every model below."),
  sum(!is.na(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4))))
```

## 12.6 Adjusted Cumulative Incidence — AKI within 1 Year (Carboplatin AUC >= 3, all patients)

Section 12.2 reports subdistribution hazard ratios; these curves give the
absolute risk the same fit implies. They are **model-standardised**: every
patient in the analysis set is assigned to one quartile in turn, their
cumulative incidence is predicted from the adjusted Fine-Gray model, and the
predictions are averaged across the cohort. A curve is therefore the incidence
the whole cohort would show if all of it sat in that quartile with the
covariate mix held fixed — not the observed curve of the patients who happen to
fall in it. Death is the competing event, so these are cumulative incidence
functions, not 1 − Kaplan-Meier.

The band is a pointwise 95 % interval from 500 bootstrap resamples of the
patients, each one refitted and re-standardised. It carries no multiplicity
correction and is not a test of the gap between quartiles — that is the
p-value in the Section 12.2 table.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-q4-cif-setup
CIF_BOOT <- 500   # bootstrap resamples behind the pointwise band

PAL_Q4 <- c("Q4 (least discordant)" = "#1F78B4", "Q3"                   = "#A6CEE3",
            "Q2"                    = "#FDBF6F", "Q1 (most discordant)" = "#E31A1C")

# g-formula standardisation. Set the quartile dummies of the fitted design
# matrix to one level for every patient, predict each patient's CIF, average
# over the cohort, then read the step function onto a common time grid so
# bootstrap replicates with different event times can be stacked.
.cif_std <- function(fitobj, lv, tg, pred) {
  X <- as.matrix(stats::model.matrix(fitobj))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(lv), function(i) {
    Xq <- X
    Xq[, grep(paste0("^", pred), colnames(Xq))] <- 0
    nm <- paste0(pred, lv[i])
    if (nm %in% colnames(Xq)) Xq[, nm] <- 1
    pr <- stats::predict(fitobj$cmprsk, cov1 = Xq)
    tibble::tibble(Quartile = factor(lv[i], levels = lv), time = tg,
      cif = stats::approx(pr[, 1], rowMeans(pr[, -1, drop = FALSE]),
                          xout = tg, method = "constant", f = 0,
                          yleft = 0, rule = 2)$y)
  }))
}

# Fit the adjusted Fine-Gray model exactly as fg_model() does, standardise it,
# and bootstrap the whole pipeline for the band.
.cif_q4 <- function(time_var, status_var, d = dat, boot = CIF_BOOT) {
  pred <- "egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4"
  # .adj_set() takes pred_var on the whole / entire pages and not on the
  # carboplatin ones, so call whichever signature this page defines.
  adj  <- if ("pred_var" %in% names(formals(.adj_set)))
            .adj_set(pred, NULL, "cre_idx") else .adj_set(NULL, "cre_idx")
  cc <- d %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(c(time_var, status_var, pred, adj)))
  fml <- stats::as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
                                  paste(c(pred, adj), collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- tidycmprsk::crr(fml, failcode = 1, data = cc)
  lv  <- levels(droplevels(cc[[pred]]))
  tg  <- seq(0, max(cc[[time_var]][cc[[status_var]] != 0]), length.out = 200)
  est <- .cif_std(fit, lv, tg, pred)
  nrw <- length(lv) * length(tg)
  bs  <- vapply(seq_len(boot), function(b) tryCatch({
      i <- sample.int(nrow(cc), nrow(cc), replace = TRUE)
      .cif_std(tidycmprsk::crr(fml, failcode = 1, data = cc[i, ]), lv, tg, pred)$cif
    }, error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, nrw)), numeric(nrw))
  ok <- colSums(is.na(bs)) == 0
  est$lo <- if (any(ok)) apply(bs[, ok, drop = FALSE], 1, stats::quantile, .025) else NA_real_
  est$hi <- if (any(ok)) apply(bs[, ok, drop = FALSE], 1, stats::quantile, .975) else NA_real_
  attr(est, "meta") <- list(n = nrow(cc), ev = sum(cc[[status_var]] == 1),
                            cmp = sum(cc[[status_var]] == 2), nb = sum(ok))
  est
}

.cif_plot <- function(x, ttl, sub) {
  m  <- attr(x, "meta")
  en <- x %>% dplyr::group_by(Quartile) %>% dplyr::slice_max(time, n = 1) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  # A bootstrap band that spans most of the 0-100 % range carries no
  # information and squashes the curves against the floor of the panel. Drop
  # it and say so, rather than draw a figure that cannot be read.
  bw   <- stats::median(x$hi - x$lo, na.rm = TRUE)
  wide <- !is.finite(bw) || bw > 0.5
  note <- if (!is.finite(bw))
      "Model-standardised; band omitted, the bootstrap did not converge"
    else if (wide)
      sprintf("Model-standardised; band omitted, %d bootstraps span %.0f points",
              m$nb, 100 * bw)
    else
      sprintf("Model-standardised; band = pointwise 95%% from %d bootstraps", m$nb)
  ggplot(x, aes(time, cif, color = Quartile, fill = Quartile)) +
    (if (wide) NULL else
       geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.13, color = NA)) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = en, aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * cif)),
      direction = "y", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 6, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
      segment.color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = PAL_Q4) + scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_Q4) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.09))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(title = ttl, subtitle = sprintf("%s | N = %d, %d events, %d competing deaths\n%s",
           sub, m$n, m$ev, m$cmp, note),
         x = "Days from baseline", y = "Adjusted cumulative incidence",
         color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

.cif_fig <- .wrap_plot(function(time_var, status_var, ttl, sub)
  .cif_plot(.cif_q4(time_var, status_var), ttl, sub))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-q4-cif-aki
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

         "Adjusted cumulative incidence of AKI within 1 year",
         "Carboplatin AUC >= 3, all patients")
```

# 13 Linear Mixed Model — Creatinine eGFR Slope over Days 0-360 (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> **What this section adds.** The 360-Day Delta eGFR section compares one number
> per patient: the median creatinine eGFR over days 271-360 minus baseline. That
> needs a creatinine in the final window, which only part of the cohort has, so
> those models are complete-case on a single difference. This section instead
> fits a **linear mixed model** to every creatinine eGFR in days 0-360, so each
> patient contributes whatever measurements they have and nobody is dropped for
> missing the last window. Both are kept — they answer related but different
> questions, and it is worth seeing whether they agree.
>
> **Data.** One row per creatinine eGFR. Day 0 is `eGFR_CRE_baseline`; every
> later row is a post-baseline creatinine inside days 1-360, read from
> `ritu_cre_traj.rds` (Section 5.16b of [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd)).
> Patients with no post-baseline creatinine in that span are not in the model.
> Time is in **years** (`time_yr = day / 365`), so every coefficient below is
> mL/min/1.73m² **per year** and **negative means decline**.
>
> **Model.** `eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * group + covariates + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)`
>
> - `time_yr × group` is the estimand — the difference in annual eGFR slope
>   between each exposure level and the reference level.
> - `group` on its own is the day-0 difference between the levels.
> - `(1 + time_yr | EMPI)` gives each patient a random intercept **and** a random
>   slope, with an unstructured 2 × 2 covariance so the model can let patients who
>   start lower decline faster or slower. Residuals are independent (σ²I); the
>   random slope already induces within-patient correlation that grows with time
>   separation. Fitted by REML in `lme4`, p-values by Satterthwaite from
>   `lmerTest`.
> - **Covariates are main effects only.** They adjust the day-0 level, not the
>   slope; only the exposure is allowed to interact with time. The covariate set
>   is otherwise the same one the Fine-Gray models use.
> - **`baseline_cre_egfr` is deliberately left out.** Day 0 of the outcome *is*
>   the baseline creatinine eGFR, so adjusting for it would mean conditioning on
>   the outcome's own first observation; the random intercept already absorbs
>   where each patient starts. Everywhere else on this page the kidney adjuster
>   is still `baseline_cre_egfr`.
> - The slope is **one straight line** across days 0-360. The observed group
>   means are close to flat for the first six months and then fall (Section
>   3.3), so a single line averages an early plateau with a later decline.
>   Read it as the average rate over the year, not as a constant one.
>
> The **Unadjusted** column fits the same model with no covariates, on the same
> patients as the adjusted model, so the two columns are directly comparable.

## 13.1 Trajectory data behind these models

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-lmm-setup
# Long-format creatinine eGFR, one row per post-baseline value in days 1-360.
# Written by ritu_data.qmd, which keeps it out of the one-row-per-patient
# masters. Keyed by EMPI only, so this page joins its own cohort to it.
lmm_traj_all <- readRDS("ritu_cre_traj.rds")

LMM_CTL <- lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

# Build the long frame for one model: the cohort's patient-level columns, a
# day-0 row carrying eGFR_CRE_baseline, then every post-baseline value. The
# day-0 anchor is eGFR_CRE_baseline, not baseline_cre_egfr -- the latter comes
# off a different creatinine draw and is not on this trajectory's scale.
.lmm_data <- function(d, vars) {
  pat <- d %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(unique(c("EMPI", "eGFR_CRE_baseline", vars)))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(eGFR_CRE_baseline)) %>%
    dplyr::semi_join(lmm_traj_all, by = "EMPI")
  post <- pat %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(lmm_traj_all %>% dplyr::select(EMPI, cre_day, eGFR_CRE),
                      by = "EMPI")
  dplyr::bind_rows(pat %>% mutate(cre_day = 0, eGFR_CRE = eGFR_CRE_baseline),
                   post) %>%
    dplyr::select(-eGFR_CRE_baseline) %>%
    mutate(time_yr = cre_day / 365) %>%
    arrange(EMPI, cre_day)
}

# egfr_adj = "none" leaves every kidney term out of the adjuster set.
.lmm_fits <- function(pred_var) {
  adj <- .adj_for(pred_var, "none")
  d   <- .lmm_data(dat, c(pred_var, adj))
  rhs <- paste0("eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * ", pred_var)
  list(pred = pred_var,
       un = lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(paste0(rhs, " + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)")),
                           data = d, control = LMM_CTL),
       ad = lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(paste0(rhs, " + ",
              paste(adj, collapse = " + "), " + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)")),
              data = d, control = LMM_CTL))
}

lmm_slope <- function(pred_var, docx_name = NULL) {
  m  <- .lmm_fits(pred_var)
  tb <- function(x) tbl_regression(
    x, pvalue_fun = function(p) style_pvalue(p, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tb(m$un), tb(m$ad)),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Unadjusted**", "**Adjusted**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  attr(out, "lmm") <- m
  out
}
lmm_slope <- .wrap_tbl(lmm_slope)

# Group-specific annual slopes implied by the adjusted fixed effects: the
# reference slope is b[time_yr], each other level's is b[time_yr] plus its
# interaction term. SEs come from the fixed-effect covariance matrix; the
# p-value is the Satterthwaite test on the interaction. Returns nothing for a
# continuous exposure (no groups) or when the fit failed and .wrap_tbl caught it.
.lmm_slope_tbl <- function(x) {
  m <- attr(x, "lmm")
  if (is.null(m)) return(invisible(NULL))
  fit <- m$ad; pred <- m$pred
  mf  <- stats::model.frame(fit)
  if (!is.factor(mf[[pred]])) return(invisible(NULL))
  b  <- lme4::fixef(fit); V <- as.matrix(stats::vcov(fit)); nm <- names(b)
  cf <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  it <- which(startsWith(nm, paste0("time_yr:", pred)))
  fmt <- function(cv) {
    e <- sum(cv * b); s <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(cv) %*% V %*% cv))
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", e, e - 1.96 * s, e + 1.96 * s)
  }
  t0 <- as.numeric(nm == "time_yr"); lv <- levels(mf[[pred]])
  rows <- list(tibble::tibble(
    Group = paste0(lv[1], " (reference)"),
    `eGFR slope, mL/min/1.73m² per year` = fmt(t0),
    `Difference vs reference` = "—", `p-value` = "—"))
  for (k in seq_along(it)) {
    cv <- t0; cv[it[k]] <- 1
    dv <- as.numeric(seq_along(nm) == it[k])
    rows[[k + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
      Group = sub(paste0("^time_yr:", pred), "", nm[it[k]]),
      `eGFR slope, mL/min/1.73m² per year` = fmt(cv),
      `Difference vs reference` = fmt(dv),
      `p-value` = style_pvalue(cf[nm[it[k]], "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3))
  }
  knitr::kable(dplyr::bind_rows(rows), caption = sprintf(paste0(
    "Adjusted annual creatinine eGFR slope by group. Negative = decline. ",
    "N = %d patients, %d eGFR values including the day-0 baseline. ",
    "The p-value tests the time x group interaction (Satterthwaite)."),
    as.integer(lme4::ngrps(fit)), stats::nobs(fit)))
}

# How much data the models actually see, next to the cohort they come from.
.lmm_n <- .lmm_data(dat, "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat")
.lmm_k <- as.integer(table(.lmm_n$EMPI)) - 1L   # minus the day-0 row
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Patients in this cohort",
               "Patients with >= 1 creatinine in days 1-360",
               "eGFR values in the model (incl. day 0)",
               "Post-baseline values per patient, median [IQR]",
               "Patients with >= 4 post-baseline values"),
  Value = c(
    as.character(nrow(dat)),
    as.character(dplyr::n_distinct(.lmm_n$EMPI)),
    as.character(nrow(.lmm_n)),
    sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(.lmm_k),
            quantile(.lmm_k, .25), quantile(.lmm_k, .75)),
    sprintf("%d (%.1f %%)", sum(.lmm_k >= 4), 100 * mean(.lmm_k >= 4)))),
  caption = paste0("Repeated creatinine eGFR available to the mixed models. ",
                   "Models are additionally complete-case on the covariates, ",
                   "so a fitted N can be slightly lower."))
```

## 13.2 Observed trajectories and fitted slopes — cut at − 10 % (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3, all patients)

Points are raw mean creatinine eGFR in 60-day bins (day 0 shown on its own),
with a 95 % CI (mean ± 1.96 × SE); bins holding fewer than 11 values are
suppressed. Lines are the
fitted population slopes from the **unadjusted** mixed model. The points are
cross-sectional means, so which patients contribute changes from bin to bin —
the lines, which use each patient's whole trajectory, are the estimate; the
points are only there to show the raw data behind it.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-lmm-traj
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
.lmm_traj_plot <- function(pred_var, ttl) {
  adj <- .adj_for(pred_var, "none")
  d   <- .lmm_data(dat, c(pred_var, adj)) %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[pred_var]]))
  fit <- lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(paste0("eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * ", pred_var,
           " + (1 + time_yr | EMPI)")), data = d, control = LMM_CTL)
  b  <- lme4::fixef(fit); lv <- levels(d[[pred_var]])
  ln <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(lv), function(k) {
    a <- b[["(Intercept)"]]; s <- b[["time_yr"]]
    if (k > 1) {
      a <- a + b[[paste0(pred_var, lv[k])]]
      s <- s + b[[paste0("time_yr:", pred_var, lv[k])]]
    }
    tibble::tibble(grp = factor(lv[k], levels = lv), cre_day = c(0, 360),
                   fit = a + s * c(0, 360) / 365)
  }))
  obs <- d %>%
    mutate(grp = .data[[pred_var]],
           mid = ifelse(cre_day == 0, 0,
                        pmin(floor(cre_day / 60), 5) * 60 + 30)) %>%
    group_by(grp, mid) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(eGFR_CRE), se = sd(eGFR_CRE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
              k = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(k >= 11)   # small-cell suppression
  ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = ln, aes(cre_day, fit, color = grp), linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_errorbar(data = obs, aes(mid, ymin = m - 1.96 * se,
                                  ymax = m + 1.96 * se, color = grp),
                  width = 8, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = obs, aes(mid, m, color = grp), size = 2.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("grey35", "#E31A1C", "#1F78B4", "#33A02C"),
                       name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 360, 60)) +
    labs(title = ttl, x = "Days from baseline",
         y = "Creatinine eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
.lmm_traj_plot <- .wrap_plot(.lmm_traj_plot)

.lmm_traj_plot("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat",
               "Creatinine eGFR over the first year, by eGFR difference (sens)")
```

percentage points further the cystatin C eGFR sits below the creatinine eGFR.
