# 14 CKD Stage Reclassification — eGFR Trends (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

> **The question.** Everyone carries two baseline CKD stages: one from the
> creatinine eGFR (`ckd_stage_cre`, from `baseline_cre_egfr`) and one from the
> CKD-EPI creatinine–cystatin C eGFR (`ckd_stage_cre_cys`, from
> `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys`), both indexed to BSA. The Sankey in the distributions
> section shows who moves between them. This section asks what happens next:
> does the creatinine eGFR fall faster in the patients cystatin C reclassifies
> into a **worse** stage?
>
> **Two groupings.**
>
> 1. **Eight groups** — within each baseline creatinine stage G1 to G3b, split
>    by whether the Cr-Cys stage is the same or better, or worse. G4 and G5 by
>    creatinine are not split this way; there are too few.
> 2. **Two groups**, across every creatinine stage — **same or better** by
>    Cr-Cys against **reclassified worse** by Cr-Cys.
>
> **What is plotted.** Mean creatinine eGFR with a 95 % confidence interval
> (mean ± 1.96 × SE) at baseline
> and at each of the four windows — `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, then the medians over
> days 1-90, 91-180, 181-270 and 271-360 built in Section 3.3. The y axis is
> the creatinine eGFR throughout; serial cystatin C is not available, so the
> Cr-Cys stage is a **baseline** grouping, not a repeated measure.
>
> **Read the lines with the composition in mind.** Each point is a
> cross-sectional mean of whoever had a creatinine in that window, and coverage
> falls from about 99 % in the first window to about 63 % in the last (Section
> 3.3). So a line can move because patients declined or because a different
> set of patients contributed. The mixed models in the previous section are the
> within-patient version of the same question.
>
> **Small cells are suppressed.** A group is plotted only when at least 11
> patients have a baseline value, and a later mark is omitted when it falls
> below 11 — so a line can stop early. Each plot names what was dropped.

## 14.1 Group definitions and sizes

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-trend-setup
# Canonical stage order, independent of which levels survive droplevels() in a
# cohort, so the groupings are built by position rather than by factor level.
CKD_LV      <- c("G1 (>=90)", "G2 (60-89)", "G3a (45-59)", "G3b (30-44)",
                 "G4 (15-29)", "G5 (<15)")
CKD_SHORT   <- c("G1", "G2", "G3a", "G3b", "G4", "G5")
TREND_MIN_N <- 11

# Labels mirror the requested list: within creatinine stage i, "same or better"
# is Cr-Cys stage <= i and "worse" is >= i+1. ASCII >= / <= throughout, matching
# the stage names themselves.
.lab_same  <- function(i) if (i == 1) "G1 cre, G1 by Cr-Cys" else
  sprintf("%s cre, <=%s by Cr-Cys", CKD_SHORT[i], CKD_SHORT[i])
.lab_worse <- function(i)
  sprintf("%s cre, >=%s by Cr-Cys", CKD_SHORT[i], CKD_SHORT[i + 1])

.ckd_groups <- function(d) {
  ci    <- match(as.character(d$ckd_stage_cre),     CKD_LV)
  yi    <- match(as.character(d$ckd_stage_cre_cys), CKD_LV)
  worse <- yi > ci
  d$ckd_shift2 <- factor(
    ifelse(worse, "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys", "Same or better by Cr-Cys"),
    levels = c("Same or better by Cr-Cys", "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys"))
  lab <- ifelse(worse,
    vapply(ci, function(i) if (is.na(i)) NA_character_ else .lab_worse(i), ""),
    vapply(ci, function(i) if (is.na(i)) NA_character_ else .lab_same(i), ""))
  lab[is.na(ci) | ci > 4] <- NA        # the eight groups stop at G3b
  d$ckd_shift8 <- factor(lab, levels = unlist(lapply(1:4,
                    function(i) c(.lab_same(i), .lab_worse(i)))))
  d
}

TREND_MARKS <- c(BL = "eGFR_CRE_baseline", "90" = "eGFR_CRE_d90",
                 "180" = "eGFR_CRE_d180", "270" = "eGFR_CRE_d270",
                 "360" = "eGFR_CRE_d360")

# Day each window closes, used to stop carrying forward at death.
TREND_CLOSE <- c(BL = 0, "90" = 90, "180" = 180, "270" = 270, "360" = 360)

# Last observation carried forward: a patient with no creatinine inside a window
# keeps the value from their most recent earlier window. Baseline is present for
# everyone in a group, so after carrying the only patients still absent from a
# mark are those who died on or before it. kc counts how many of a mark's values
# are carried rather than measured in that window.
.trend_stats <- function(d, grp_var) {
  mk <- names(TREND_MARKS)
  v  <- lapply(TREND_MARKS, function(cl) d[[cl]])
  names(v) <- mk
  dd <- if ("death_days_any" %in% names(d)) d$death_days_any else
          rep(NA_real_, nrow(d))
  cf <- stats::setNames(lapply(mk, function(.) rep(FALSE, nrow(d))), mk)
  for (j in seq_along(mk)[-1]) {
    g <- is.na(v[[j]]) & !is.na(v[[j - 1]]) &
         (is.na(dd) | dd > TREND_CLOSE[[mk[j]]])
    v[[j]][g]  <- v[[j - 1]][g]
    cf[[j]][g] <- TRUE
  }
  st <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mk), function(j)
      tibble::tibble(grp = d[[grp_var]], day = mk[j],
                     egfr = v[[j]], carried = cf[[j]]))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(grp), !is.na(egfr)) %>%
    mutate(day = factor(day, levels = mk)) %>%
    group_by(grp, day) %>%
    summarise(m = mean(egfr), se = sd(egfr) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
              k = dplyr::n(), kc = sum(carried), .groups = "drop")
  keep <- st %>% filter(day == "BL", k >= TREND_MIN_N) %>% pull(grp)
  list(stats   = st %>% filter(grp %in% keep, k >= TREND_MIN_N) %>% droplevels(),
       dropped = st %>% filter(day == "BL", k < TREND_MIN_N) %>%
                   transmute(grp = as.character(grp), n = k),
       thin    = sum(st$grp %in% keep & st$k < TREND_MIN_N))
}

PAL8 <- c(G1 = "#1F78B4", G2 = "#33A02C", G3a = "#FF7F00", G3b = "#E31A1C")
PAL2 <- c("Same or better by Cr-Cys" = "#1F78B4",
          "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys" = "#E31A1C")

# by_stage = TRUE colours by creatinine stage and dashes the reclassified-worse
# line, so the eight groups read as four pairs.
trend_plot <- function(grp_var, ttl, by_stage = FALSE) {
  r  <- .trend_stats(.ckd_groups(dat), grp_var)
  st <- r$stats
  if (!nrow(st)) stop("no group reaches the minimum cell size in this cohort")
  st <- st %>% mutate(
    cre   = factor(sub(" cre.*", "", as.character(grp)), levels = CKD_SHORT),
    shift = ifelse(grepl(">=", as.character(grp), fixed = TRUE),
                   "Worse by Cr-Cys", "Same or better"))
  note <- c(
    paste("Last observation carried forward: a patient with no creatinine in a",
          "window keeps their most recent earlier value, and carrying stops at",
          "death. Bracketed counts in the table below are carried values."),
    if (nrow(r$dropped)) sprintf("Not plotted, fewer than %d patients: %s.",
      TREND_MIN_N, paste(sprintf("%s (n = %d)", r$dropped$grp, r$dropped$n),
                         collapse = "; ")),
    if (r$thin) sprintf("%d later mark(s) also fall below %d and are omitted.",
                        r$thin, TREND_MIN_N))
  key <- if (by_stage) "cre" else "grp"
  p <- ggplot(st, aes(day, m, group = grp, colour = .data[[key]])) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - 1.96 * se, ymax = m + 1.96 * se),
                  width = .12, linewidth = .5) +
    {if (by_stage) geom_line(aes(linetype = shift), linewidth = .9)
     else geom_line(linewidth = .9)} +
    geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = if (by_stage) PAL8 else PAL2,
                        name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
    labs(title = ttl, x = "Days from baseline",
         y = "Creatinine eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²)", linetype = NULL,
         caption = if (length(note)) paste(
           strwrap(paste(note, collapse = " "), width = 115), collapse = "\n")
           else NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
  attr(p, "counts") <- st %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cell = ifelse(kc > 0, sprintf("%d (%d)", k, kc),
                                as.character(k))) %>%
    dplyr::select(grp, day, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = day, values_from = cell) %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group = grp)
  p
}
trend_plot <- .wrap_plot(trend_plot)

# Per-mark n behind the plot above it. Silent when the plot failed to build.
trend_counts <- function(p) {
  k <- attr(p, "counts")
  if (is.null(k)) return(invisible(NULL))
  # The cells are strings now ("215 (69)"), and kable's na= does not blank a
  # character column, so clear the suppressed ones here.
  k[] <- lapply(k, function(cl) {
    cl <- as.character(cl); cl[is.na(cl)] <- ""; cl })
  knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(k, "counts"), caption = paste0(
    "Patients contributing to each mark; (n) = how many of them carry forward ",
    "an earlier window's value rather than one measured in that window. ",
    "Blank = fewer than ", TREND_MIN_N, " and not plotted."))
}

.g_all  <- .ckd_groups(dat)
.g_surv <- .ckd_groups(dat %>% filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up),
                                      days_last_follow_up > 365))
.cnt <- function(a, b, v) {
  ta <- table(a[[v]]); tb <- table(b[[v]])
  tibble::tibble(Group = names(ta), `All patients` = as.integer(ta),
                 Survivors = as.integer(tb[names(ta)])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Survivors = ifelse(is.na(Survivors), 0L, Survivors),
                  Plotted = ifelse(`All patients` >= TREND_MIN_N, "yes", "no"))
}
knitr::kable(.cnt(.g_all, .g_surv, "ckd_shift8"), caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Eight groups: baseline creatinine stage crossed with whether Cr-Cys puts ",
  "the patient in a worse stage. Cohort N = %d."), nrow(dat)))
knitr::kable(.cnt(.g_all, .g_surv, "ckd_shift2"), caption = paste0(
  "Two groups, every baseline creatinine stage included."))
```

# 15 Baseline-Matched eGFR Trends (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

The Section 14 plots start from different levels: inside every baseline
creatinine stage the reclassified-worse group sits lower, because cystatin C
pushes a patient out of a stage band most easily when they already sit near its
floor. A difference in where two lines end is therefore partly a difference in
where they began. This section repeats those four plots on a matched cohort, so
each pair of lines starts from the same baseline creatinine eGFR.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-match-setup
MATCH_CAL <- 2   # caliper on baseline creatinine eGFR, mL/min/1.73m2

# Greedy 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on baseline creatinine eGFR. Each
# reclassified-worse patient takes the same-or-better patient closest to it,
# among those inside MATCH_CAL and in the same baseline creatinine CKD stage.
# Controls are used once. Treated patients with the fewest eligible controls go
# first, which maximises the number of pairs. Returns the matched rows only.
.match_bl <- function(d) {
  g  <- .ckd_groups(d)
  ci <- match(as.character(g$ckd_stage_cre), CKD_LV)
  bl <- g$eGFR_CRE_baseline
  w  <- !is.na(g$ckd_shift2) &
        g$ckd_shift2 == "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys"
  ok <- !is.na(ci) & ci <= 4 & !is.na(bl) & !is.na(g$ckd_shift2)
  tr <- which(ok & w); co <- which(ok & !w)
  if (!length(tr) || !length(co)) return(g[0, , drop = FALSE])
  elig <- lapply(tr, function(i)
    co[abs(bl[co] - bl[i]) <= MATCH_CAL & ci[co] == ci[i]])
  names(elig) <- as.character(tr)
  used <- integer(0); a <- integer(0); b <- integer(0)
  for (i in tr[order(lengths(elig))]) {
    cand <- setdiff(elig[[as.character(i)]], used)
    if (!length(cand)) next
    pick <- cand[which.min(abs(bl[cand] - bl[i]))]
    used <- c(used, pick); a <- c(a, i); b <- c(b, pick)
  }
  if (!length(a)) return(g[0, , drop = FALSE])
  out <- g[c(a, b), , drop = FALSE]
  out$.pair_id <- rep(seq_along(a), 2)
  out
}

# Baseline creatinine eGFR in the two groups before and after matching, with the
# standardised mean difference.
.match_balance <- function(d) {
  sm <- function(x, y) (mean(x) - mean(y)) / sqrt((var(x) + var(y)) / 2)
  row <- function(lbl, f) {
    if (!nrow(f)) return(NULL)
    w <- f$ckd_shift2 == "Reclassified worse by Cr-Cys"
    a <- f$eGFR_CRE_baseline[w & !is.na(f$eGFR_CRE_baseline)]
    b <- f$eGFR_CRE_baseline[!w & !is.na(f$eGFR_CRE_baseline)]
    if (length(a) < 2 || length(b) < 2) return(NULL)
    tibble::tibble(Set = lbl,
      `Worse n` = length(a), `Worse mean` = round(mean(a), 1),
      `Same or better n` = length(b), `Same or better mean` = round(mean(b), 1),
      Difference = round(mean(a) - mean(b), 1), SMD = round(sm(a, b), 3))
  }
  g <- .ckd_groups(d) %>%
    filter(!is.na(ckd_shift2), !is.na(eGFR_CRE_baseline),
           !is.na(match(as.character(ckd_stage_cre), CKD_LV[1:4])))
  dplyr::bind_rows(row("Before matching", g),
                   row("After matching",  .match_bl(d)))
}
.match_balance <- .wrap_tbl(.match_balance)
```

## 15.1 Matching method

1. **Eligible patients** — baseline creatinine CKD stage G1 to G3b, a known
   CKD-EPI creatinine–cystatin C stage, and a non-missing baseline creatinine
   eGFR. G4 and G5 are not matched; there are too few.
2. **Groups** — *reclassified worse by Cr-Cys* is the treated group, *same or
   better by Cr-Cys* the control pool, exactly as in Section PREV15.
3. **Matching variable** — baseline creatinine eGFR (`eGFR_CRE_baseline`), the
   quantity the two groups differ on at day 0.
4. **Caliper** — a control must be within **2 mL/min/1.73m²** of the treated
   patient's baseline creatinine eGFR.
5. **Exact stratum** — the control must also be in the **same baseline
   creatinine CKD stage**, so no pair straddles a stage boundary.
6. **Ratio** — 1:1, **without replacement**; each control is used at most once.
7. **Choice inside the caliper** — nearest neighbour on baseline creatinine
   eGFR.
8. **Order** — treated patients with the fewest eligible controls are matched
   first, which maximises the number of pairs formed.
9. **Unmatched patients are dropped**, treated and control alike.
10. **Balance check** — Section 15.2 gives the standardised mean difference
    before and after. |SMD| < 0.1 is the usual threshold for adequate balance.

The five windows, the carry-forward rule and the small-cell suppression at 11
are unchanged from Section PREV15.

> **What this fixes, and what it does not.** Matching removes the baseline gap
> and leaves the exposure intact — baseline cystatin C stays far apart after
> matching, because reclassification is defined by cystatin C being high
> *relative to* creatinine. It does **not** balance comorbidity (Charlson stays
> higher in the reclassified-worse group), it does not repair the window
> attrition described in Section 14, and it discards every patient who
> cannot be paired. Read these plots beside Section 13 rather than in place
> of it: the mixed model keeps every patient and every value, and its random
> intercept already absorbs the baseline level matched on here.

## 15.7 Slope over days 0-360 against days 90-360 (Carboplatin AUC >= 3, matched)

The matched gap in 15.5 opens almost entirely between baseline and day 90 and
is then flat. Progressive decline would widen the gap steadily; a step that
appears at once and plateaus is what differential regression to the mean looks
like, since the matched controls were picked for an unusually low reading and
part of that is transient.

This fits the same random-intercept, random-slope model twice on the matched
cohort — over days 0–360, then over days 90–360 with the first step excluded.
Slopes are mL/min/1.73m² per year; the difference is reclassified-worse minus
same-or-better, so a negative value means the worse group falls faster. If the
day-0 to 90 step is driving the result, the difference shrinks towards zero in
the days 90–360 rows.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-auc3-match-post90
# Mixed model on the matched cohort over a chosen day range. from_day = 0 keeps
# the baseline anchor as day 0; from_day = 90 drops it and every value before
# day 90, so the fit sees only the post-step part of the trajectory.
.match_slope <- function(d, from_day) {
  pat <- .match_bl(d) %>%
    dplyr::select(EMPI, ckd_shift2, eGFR_CRE_baseline) %>%
    filter(!is.na(ckd_shift2), !is.na(eGFR_CRE_baseline))
  post <- pat %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(lmm_traj_all %>% dplyr::select(EMPI, cre_day, eGFR_CRE),
                      by = "EMPI") %>%
    filter(cre_day >= from_day, cre_day <= 360)
  lf <- if (from_day == 0)
          dplyr::bind_rows(
            pat %>% mutate(cre_day = 0, eGFR_CRE = eGFR_CRE_baseline), post)
        else post
  lf <- lf %>% mutate(time_yr = cre_day / 365) %>% droplevels()
  lmerTest::lmer(eGFR_CRE ~ time_yr * ckd_shift2 + (1 + time_yr | EMPI),
                 data = lf, control = LMM_CTL)
}

# One row: each group's annual slope, their difference, and the Satterthwaite
# test on the interaction.
.slope_row <- function(d, from_day, lbl) {
  fit <- .match_slope(d, from_day)
  b  <- lme4::fixef(fit); cf <- summary(fit)$coefficients; nm <- names(b)
  it <- grep("^time_yr:ckd_shift2", nm, value = TRUE)[1]
  if (is.na(it)) return(NULL)
  est <- cf[it, "Estimate"]; se <- cf[it, "Std. Error"]
  tibble::tibble(
    Cohort = lbl,
    Days = if (from_day == 0) "0-360" else "90-360",
    Patients = as.integer(lme4::ngrps(fit)[["EMPI"]]),
    Values = as.integer(stats::nobs(fit)),
    `Same or better` = sprintf("%.1f", b[["time_yr"]]),
    `Reclassified worse` = sprintf("%.1f", b[["time_yr"]] + est),
    `Difference (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)",
                                    est, est - 1.96 * se, est + 1.96 * se),
    `p-value` = style_pvalue(cf[it, "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 3))
}

.post90_table <- function() {
  surv <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    .slope_row(dat,  0,  "All patients"),
    .slope_row(dat,  90, "All patients"),
    .slope_row(surv, 0,  "Survivors"),
    .slope_row(surv, 90, "Survivors"))
}
.post90_table <- .wrap_tbl(.post90_table)

knitr::kable(.tbl_docx(.post90_table()), caption = paste0(
  "Annual creatinine eGFR slope in the matched cohort, over days 0-360 and ",
  "over days 90-360. Difference is reclassified-worse minus same-or-better; ",
  "negative means the worse group falls faster."))
```
